reviews.content: i really enjoyed this class a lot more than the french class i took in the previous semester (composition and conversation with karen santos da silva). professor suter doesn't force students to talk if they don't want to and makes an effort to keep people engaged by cracking some jokes and asking students what their ideas about the readings are. although i wasn't super interested in literary and artistic movements before this class, so i sometimes wouldn't know what my classmates were referencing, i think professor suter does a really good job in making sure that everyone is on the same page as well as making it interesting for people who had never had previous exposure to this type of information. i would recommend taking this class. it's def a more lecture style, which surprised me a bit since my other class was super conversational, but professor suter does have times where she makes you break off into groups to discuss the readings so you can also practice your speaking skills.
reviews.workload: a presentation about a woman writer/painter in left bank culture (you choose during the first few classes) and a written version of your presentation, participation (mostly based on attendance i think; she does take attendance each class and learns everyone's name pretty fast), an in class written midterm (prompt for my year was you meet a reporter and you have to tell them about what you've learned in the class so far and mention the contributions of 8 women in left bank culture and then propose an article idea), a final paper, and an explication de texte over a reading that you choose to do. some of the readings can be a bit dense but professor suter does a good job at summarizing them in class and talking about them enough that you don't need to understand everything when you read it. also, i think she gives most people A's for the writing assignments except for explication de texte and final papers where she varies the grades but generally I think she's a pretty easy grader.

reviews.content: She is a phenomenal professor and this is a very interesting course. Mostly discussions with a little bit of lecturing, very interesting and mostly quick content.
reviews.workload:
A 3 page analysis of a text, a presentation (written and visual) on an important historical figure from the period of your choice, one written exam and one end of the semester dissertation, plus weekly reading. 

The reading is easy to get through, and although this sounds like a lot, it really isn't. Hadley is a fair grader and a very understanding person who will readily accommodate your needs. Take this class!!

reviews.content: Postlewate is an incredible professor who really cares about her students. The work load was more than manageable throughout the semster, though she expects you to go back to your midterms during finals and continue to make edits which can feel a bit overwhelming. She’s incredibly flexible and really gave us the time we needed to get stuff in on our own time.
reviews.workload: Two midterm translation projects with preface written by you. You're expected to come back to these midterms during finals period with another round of edits. Finals project is a personal translation project.

reviews.content: Going into class, I was nervous because I had 0 experience with Italian. Prof. Gozzi made me feel super comfortable and has really taught me a lot. The class is actually very fun; we do Kahoot, watch videos, and listen to songs. There are quizzes and writing assignments, but we are always very well prepared beforehand and always know exactly when the quiz will be and what the content on the quiz will be. If you want a fun, Italian class to take, absolutely sign up for Prof. Gozzi.
reviews.workload:
Attendance & Participation - 15%; Homework - 15%; Quizzes - 25%; Written production - 15%; Final Oral Exam - 10%; Final Written Exam - 20%.
Homeworks are very straightforward. Quizzes are also pretty simple; she walks around during the quiz and corrects us as we work, which helps our grades. There is a lot of vocab and grammar to learn, but nothing insane--pretty standard for a language class.

reviews.content: Going into this class, I was scared because I knew basically 0 Italian. However, Professor Federica is the absolutely best teacher! She has been my favorite teacher at Columbia so far. Her lesson plans consist of slides and activities. The class is very engaging and we interact a lot with our classmates to help practice our Italian. She is extremely passionate and welcoming. She prioritizes learning and doesn't care or get mad when you make mistakes. Overall, I would highly recommend taking Italian if she is your professor.
reviews.workload: We had a couple of written homework assignments, but all very manageable and easy if you pay attention in class. As with any language, repetition is key. She uses an online platform and assigns a lot of small homework assignments on there, but they assigned early and are due the day before each quiz. Quizzes were every 2 weeks or so, not bad at all. Our final was a project that was fun to make and incorporated everything we learned. It was a pretty easy A for me.

reviews.content: I was really looking forward to taking Calculus III and I was especially happy to take it with Professor Ivanov. He is phenomenal at teaching and explains all of the concepts thoroughly, making even difficult material much easier to understand. The lectures are fairly fast-paced. He always writes out the most important concepts separately, which is very helpful for preparing cheat sheets. He is always very helpful and is one of the best calculus professors I’ve had.
reviews.workload: Homework assignments and practice exams can be time-consuming but they are very useful in reinforcing the concepts and preparing for exams.

reviews.content: This class was honestly not that bad at all. If you attend lecture and do the homeworks/excercises, you will be just fine and get a good grade. From what I have heard, Bhat is the easiest Calc 3 teacher. That being said, he is not a GOOD teacher. He is the kind of teacher that is very smart but does not realize that we are not all as smart. He writes things down on the board and just expects you to understand them. If you ask a clarifying question, he will just repeat what he said before, but louder. However, TAs and other math resources at Columbia were much more helpful.
reviews.workload: There is a homework each week that takes less than an hour. He drops the lowest two. There are two midterms that are 25% each and a final that is 30%. If your final grade is higher than either midterm it will replace that midterm. The tests are the exact same questions as hw/exercises/class examples with different numbers. You also get a cheat sheet for all of them.

reviews.content: I thought this was gonna be a hard class coming in as a freshman. De Silva was genuinely one of the best math teachers I've ever had. She's extremely nice and helpful, and she wants the best for all her students and wants to see everyone do well. Quizzes were literally like problems picked from the accuracy section of the HW, and she would tell you which problems to look at, and she wouldn't even change the numbers, so it was super easy. Midterms were harder than the practice ones, but like still not hard to do well on, same for the final. The only issue with this class would be the 8:40 timing, definitely worth it, but if you're like me and can barely wake up, it's kinda hard to get the content from the lecture if you don't go since it's all on the chalkboard and her notes are kinda hard to follow. I was able to not go to every lecture, and I have an A in the class (Possible A+). I believe she mentioned curving at the beginning of the semester, but I'm not sure.

15 homework problems a week (10 completion, 5 accuracy), and she tells u which are for accuracy sometimes. (10% of final grade)
3 quizzes (10% of final grade) (1-2 questions pulled from the accuracy section of the homework). She cancelled the last quiz and just made one of the homeworks fully accuracy-based, though.

reviews.content: Mediocre instructor. Gets ahead of lecture sometimes and is very surprised why there's so many questions. Posted lecture notes is a game of deciphering Minecraft Enchanting Table language.
reviews.workload: I'm certain the problems he goes over in class are different than the ones he assigns for homework, which is different than the midterm practice problems, which is different than the actual exams. Problem is that what he goes over is trivially simple compared to the ones you do outside the classroom. Drops 1 HW (worth 20%), Final Exam (30%) replaces lowest Midterm 1 or 2 (25% each). You're better off reading the textbook than going to lecture.

reviews.content: Best Professor ever. In this school it's so difficult to find any professor without any minor annoyance, but Daniela is your exception. At the beginning of the semester I went to both her her and Piechnik's class just to see which one is better. I immediately dropped Piechnik's class and registered for De Silva's, for the obvious reasons. Despite her class being at 8:40am and throughout the semester it was always a life-and-death fight on the Monday/Weds mornings, I never once regretted taking this class cause her warming personality and caring to every student cure everything in me. I think one of the reasons she's so good is because her daughter is also a senior, so she knows exactly what level us freshmen are at. The contents are pretty OK, just what you would expect it to be: a little challenging but once you studied a little then it's fine.
reviews.workload:
Psets every week except the week with midterms. For most times half are graded on accuracy half are graded on completion. Sometimes she tells you which are graded on accuracy sometimes she doesn't, but it's fine cause you can check the answers on your own as they are all available online. I'm personally a slow person with math cause I enjoy doing them and it's fine for me to spend a lot of time on them. Maybe takes like 3h for me to do them but i know most people finish them under 2. 
HW & Quizes(straight from the Psets) = 20%
Midterm with better score 25%, other one 15%
Finals 40%

reviews.content: Jean Paul is the best ever! If you're lucky enough to have him as a voice teacher you're in for a real treat. My lessons with him are the highlight of my week, we have loads of fun and I learn so much. I have learned more about my voice and how to use it in my time with him than ever in my life (I've been taking voice lessons for most of it) and I have grown so much. He's so knowledgeable and finds such smart ways to imbue technical skills into technique through fun exercises. He's also super fun and great to chat with. I simply cannot recommend him enough, if an opportunity presents itself to you to work with him in any capacity, take it!
reviews.workload: Nothing official, just practice whatever songs you're working on but he's very understanding about times when you're busy and can't practice as much as you'd like to.

reviews.content:
I enjoyed the class, learned how to write a really good lab report. Prof. Brotherton, although a little awkward, he is really nice and wants you to succeed. He is passionate about both teaching and his work. Topics we looked at are interesting (political, social psychology). We never took our own data, just analyzed prior data, so if you want something more hands on, then this is not really the class for you. 

We leave class 30-45 minutes early on average
reviews.workload: Split into 3 parts, Each part has a lab report and presentation for the report. You do the parts in groups, the presentation and topic but you write your lab report on your own. Not a rigorous class, he isn't knit picky on small things and he is very encouraging.

reviews.content:
I had high hopes for this class - really high hopes. It was dreadful, because he was dreadful. I expected to do some sort of hands-on activities throughout the semester, and eventually go into a research project - that was not the case. We did a "make believe" proposal, so you don't actually get to try mimicking research; you just pretend you'll do research and write the same exact paper about 10 different times. It's incredibly boring. 
Prof's teaching style is droning and repetitive - people treated his class like office hours, asking redundant and pointless questions which he takes 20 min to address each time. He doesn't make his rubrics clear, his feedback is harsh and unclear/unhelpful, and he takes the entire 3 hour period every time. 
The content would be interesting if we actually covered any of what we learn in lecture. The one time we had an interesting lab was when we learned about the Milgram Shock experiments, and then this Prof. said those were invalid studies that didn't prove anything! Which flat out contradicted what we learned in lecture.
reviews.workload: There's one assignment every week which is basically writing and rewriting the same make-believe-research paper. It was due the next day after class at 5pm. In class, he adds on "things he's looking for", so you can't reasonably begin the assignment until after your class period. This is a really pointless lab, and I was incredibly disappointed. Take Psych of Learning lab with Ken Light instead!

reviews.content:
This class just traumatized me lol. This is no commentary on Kate personally, but the whole ordeal, from start to finish, had me in at least three stupid nervous breakdowns. I never wrote a single review on here, but I legit haven't been able to share this experience in terms of the alienating pain I felt with anyone other than my mom lol. 

I do not remember the last time I cried this much over a class, maybe it was just my karma. I variously spent hours working on assignments after lab because I did not have a good grip on SPSS at the time, having taken stats years prior. The final project was a final blow to my self-esteem. My group members and I did not have sufficient time to thoroughly go over our specific parts before Thanksgiving break for different reasons (underestimating the technicalities of SPSS analyses we'd have to conduct in a few days thereafter). Well, they smartly managed it in the end, but I ****ed up big-time, spending hours in the library confidently working on my ~results~ only to very awkwardly discover that I had done my whole part wrong as we were tying things together last minute. IT DID NOT help matters that my group members just proceeded to eye me awkwardly and designate me with a last-min easy part for the presentation, and then later that night delete the powerpoint artwork I tried to contribute to the powerpoint. And next morning, they just shunned me lol. In the end, I believe they collectively rated me w like a 3/5 for participation (Kate distributes these surveys after every ~collaboration~). 

ANYWAY, in the end I got an overall grade of B. But did I come out of this with new confidence about how I might be working in collaborative or teamwork situations in the work environment? Big no. I'm just afraid, and I wish this class could have been a better learning experience. While I understand most of my problems here are unfortunately personal, I think that, at least with the final project, there should have been a less compressed time allotment (with regard to the holidays), so that we could independently work things out or individually seek Kate's time for assistance. I did not expect to finish this class with an A, but I also did not expect to finish feeling like I sh*t my pants in public and would probably avoid all people involved in future scenarios.
reviews.workload: Please take stats before taking Barnard psych lab courses

reviews.content: Kate is an incredibly kind and brilliant scholar in psychology. Her niceness made her high grading standards a bit surprising. I would not say she is an unreasonable grader, but I think she demands a type of perfection and accuracy that other lab instructors might not. If you take this lab, prepare to go above and beyond to get an A or even a B. That being said, she makes course material interesting and explains concepts very clearly so that even people without psych backgrounds can understand.
reviews.workload: Literature review (3-5pg), method and results section based on an in-class study (2pg), observational field study group project and write-up, final research experiment/study with a group presentation and individual paper. Reasonable for a lab IMO

reviews.content: As a person who was TERRIFIED of taking a lab course, I can say that I am pretty glad I took this class because I didn't have to immerse myself in the discipline to do well.  That being said, in order to do well we had to do an extraordinary amount of busy work, which was my main problem.  Davis has all of these stupid specifications about powerpoint slides and shit that we're expected to follow which kind of defeats the purpose of being a college student if you ask me.  I feel like he'd give seniors in high school a notebook check quiz.  Anyway, my first impression of him was that he was really nice, which is true-- he's just also weirdly attention-seeking and annoying.  The epithet "well-intentioned" appears a lot in these reviews; I guess I'd second that.  Whatever.  Take this class for the lab requirement I guess, but be prepared to fall asleep during some of the most boring-ass 3 hour lectures EVER, be sure to ask him questions DURING CLASS BECAUSE HE TAKES 19088Q97W DAYS to answer his emails, and don't work with a group of people who you know will be unreliable, because you have all of this pointless shit due each week that takes a few hours to do.
reviews.workload: a bunch of shit due each week; powerpoint presentation; final research paper at the end (mostly putting together your results and pieces you handed in previously)

reviews.content: Prof Roberts is such an angel! She genuinely cares so deeply about her students inside and out of the classroom. Her classes can get pretty mundane and boring but it is all because she really aims to give everyone a base-level understanding of every assignment and concept, which often means going over pretty basic concepts a lot like defining a mean and median.
reviews.workload: Exceptionally light. Maybe an hour a week if that, until the last two or so classes when out "final projects" were due and their multiple stages of drafts (probably 2 hours a week for the last two weeks, but nothing remotely difficult).

reviews.content: I love Professor Roberts! She is kind and clearly cares a lot about her class and students (in her own words this is her "dream job"). This class was a good mix of individual and group work and, as someone who often finds science intimidating, the class material was extremely approachable and felt very doable. The Excel analysis was probably the trickiest part, but I appreciate that we usually have class time to work on assignments and so it's easy to ask questions and know if "you're doing it right" rather than being stuck in confusion.
reviews.workload:
Very light workload. Typically able to finish assignments during class time. Only exceptions are that at the beginning of the semester, need to spend about an hour on data collection outside of class, and at the end of the semester there is a research proposal assignment that is written outside of class. 
No tests, attendance tracked.

reviews.content: Professor Roberts is so lovely! She's very very organized and speaks with so much clarity regarding material and course objectives. Since this an intro lab she does not expect proficient understanding of concepts; she's super understanding. Sometimes we got let out early, which is nice given that the course is 3 hours long. She gave us plenty of time to do assignments and is very knowledgeable!
reviews.workload: Behavioral observation assignment towards the beginning, other in-class group assignments using ANOVA tools, and a final research proposal project. Sometimes the workload felt a little more than what was appropriate for a 1.5 credit class, but it wasn't anything crazy.

reviews.content: Prof. Roberts is great! She's super kind and understanding, and always checked in with students to make sure the workload wasn't too much. Additionally, she kindly wrote me a rec letter and gave very little outside of lab work.
reviews.workload: Very straightforward work, def recommend it! The only issue I had was with one assignment that required excel, but I was able to figure it out relatively easily.
